To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) in make-to-stock, the manufacturer and retailer benefit from sharing forecast information, and the retailer is better off than in the case where there is no forecast sharing and no direct channel; (b) in make-to-order, the manufacturer and whole supply chain benefit from forecast sharing, but the retailer may be worse off; and (c) the presence of a direct channel has a detrimental impact on the retailer, but may be beneficial to the manufacturer and the supply chain as a whole.

(i) in a make-to-order setting, demand forecast information sharing between the manufacturer and the traditional retailer is beneficial to the supply chain, (ii) in a make-tostock setting, demand forecast sharing is beneficial to the manufacturer and the supply chain but not necessarily to the traditional retailer, (iii) in the make-to-order and make-to-stock scenarios, the manufacturer can benefit from the direct channel, (iv) the direct channel can benefit the supply chain, but only under some conditions.
the manufacturer and the entire supply chain are better when the direct channel is added to the traditional channel.
